html: TRP channels are the airway's irritant sensors. Of the channels tested against particulate matter, two respond to the particle itself. TRPV1 is the strongest responder to coal fly ash, and TRPA1 is activated by insoluble particle material through a route distinct from the soluble electrophiles it also senses. When the particle surface binds either channel it opens a calcium-permeable pore. The calcium that enters drives the inflammatory cytokine response of the bronchial epithelium and feeds the cell's wider calcium-handling machinery. Human airway genetics support both channels, as variants of each track with asthma symptom control in people exposed to pollution.
